mainTopic: כותי witnesses on a גט, and documents made in non-Jewish courts
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a גט signed by a כותי witness. The גמרא explains that such a גט is valid because the Jewish witness signed after the כותי. On a גט the witnesses must sign together, so the Jew knowingly accepted him. רב אשי says this signing rule is a גזירה because of a husband who tells 'all of you' to sign. Next the גמרא studies רבי אלעזר's rule that only one כותי witness is allowed. It answers a challenge from the story of רבן גמליאל in two ways: אביי reads the story as 'its witness', and רבא says רבן גמליאל disagrees. A new משנה then teaches that documents from non-Jewish courts are valid, except a גט and a document freeing a slave, while רבי שמעון accepts even those. The גמרא asks how a gift document from such a court can work. It answers with שמואל's rule, דינא דמלכותא דינא, or by reading the exception as 'documents like a גט'. Finally it explains רבי שמעון through רבי אלעזר's view that the witnesses to the handing over make the divorce. After a challenge from רבי אבא, the גמרא starts narrowing the case, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Jew would only let a trustworthy כותי sign before him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation: the Jewish witness signed after the כותי, and he would not have allowed that unless the כותי was a careful, trustworthy חבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if the כותי were not a חבר, the Jew would not have let him sign before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing its answer about the משנה. The case is one where the Jewish witness signed below the כותי, and that shows the כותי can be trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jew's signature underneath works like a stamp of approval. He would not have signed after someone who is not a valid witness. So in this case we may rely on the כותי's signature.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan; usually not trusted as a witness
Someone known to keep מצוות carefully
Lets someone sign
Before him, meaning above him on the document

phrases.english: For if it were not that the Samaritan was a ḥaver,
he would not have let him sign before him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier answer, which explained the משנה as a case where the Jew signed last
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the Jew signed after the כותי
steps.terutzMaskana: A כותי who signed above a Jew is presumed to be a חבר

steps.title: Then other documents should be valid too
steps.stepSummary: If the Jew signing after the כותי proves he is trustworthy, the same logic should make other שטרות valid as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then other documents should be valid too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The משנה only made an exception for a גט and a document freeing a slave, but the reasoning seems to work for every document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the Jew's signature has nothing to do with divorce in particular. So why does the משנה say that other שטרות with a כותי witness are invalid? The answer must explain what is special about a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; this opens a challenge
Other legal documents

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ שְׁאָר שְׁטָרוֹת נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, even other documents too!
phrases.notes: He means: other documents should also be valid, yet the משנה says they are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ שְׁאָר שְׁטָרוֹת נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 1 by pointing out that it should apply more widely
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof from the Jew's signature is not special to a גט, so it should make all שטרות valid, against the משנה

steps.title: On other documents, he may have left space for an elder
steps.stepSummary: On other שטרות, the Jew's signing last proves nothing. He may have left the top spot empty out of respect for an older witness, and then the כותי signed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we say: he left space for someone older than him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the proof does not work for other documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Signing on the second line does not show that the Jew approved of whoever ended up on the first line. He may have kept that line free for an older person, and the כותי filled it later. So his signature says nothing about the כותי.

keyTerms.meaning: Space, room
He left
Older, an elder

phrases.english: Rather, we say:
he left space for one who is older than him;
phrases.notes: He kept the top line free out of respect, and then the כותי came and signed there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמְרִינַן רַוְוחָא שְׁבַק לְמַאן דְּקַשִּׁישׁ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by showing why the proof fails for other documents
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers another explanation for why the Jew signed second
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Signing after the כותי always proves he is trustworthy
steps.terutzMaskana: On ordinary שטרות, the Jew may have left room for an elder, so nothing is proven

steps.title: The same worry should apply to a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: on a גט too, perhaps the Jew left space for an elder. So why is a גט any different?
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, he may have left space for someone older than him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer from step 3 against the משנה's exception for a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If leaving space for an elder breaks the proof on other שטרות, it should break the proof on a גט as well. Then there is no reason a גט with a כותי witness should be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; used to apply the same logic to this case

phrases.english: Here too,
he left space for one who is older than him!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, רַוְוחָא שְׁבַק לְמַאן דְּקַשִּׁישׁ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from step 3 to challenge the special rule for a גט
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between a גט and other שטרות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'left space for an elder' explanation applies just as well to a גט

steps.title: Witnesses on a גט must sign together
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from the משנה that the witnesses on a גט must sign in each other's presence. That means the Jew saw the כותי sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This shows that the witnesses of a גט do not sign one without the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by showing what is special about a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses on a גט sign at the same sitting, so the Jew knew exactly who was signing above him. If he still signed, he must have accepted the כותי as a valid witness. On other שטרות, witnesses may sign at separate times, so that proof does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows; a rule learned from the source
The witnesses who sign a גט
One without the other

steps.whatToRemember: A גט with a כותי witness above a Jewish witness is valid because witnesses on a גט sign together, so the Jew knowingly accepted the כותי. Other שטרות have no such rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical rule: the witnesses on a גט must sign in each other's presence.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: That is to say,

phrases.aramaic: עֵדֵי הַגֵּט אֵין חוֹתְמִין זֶה בְּלֹא זֶה.
phrases.english: the witnesses of a bill of divorce do not sign one without the other.
phrases.notes: He means each witness signs while the other one is there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by pointing to a signing rule that is special to a גט
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a halachic difference between a גט and other שטרות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גט and other שטרות are signed the same way
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses on a גט sign together, so the Jew's signature proves he accepted the כותי

steps.title: Why must the witnesses on a גט sign together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב פפא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next step by asking where this rule about signing together comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually two separate signatures are enough for a document, so why does a גט need both witnesses present together? The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רב פפא's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason witnesses on a גט must sign in each other's presence

steps.title: A גזירה because of 'all of you'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the rule is a rabbinic גזירה. It protects the case where the husband said 'all of you' should sign, where every witness is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is a decree because of 'all of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question: the חכמים made a general rule so that a specific problem case would not go wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband says 'all of you' should sign, the גט is invalid unless every one of them signs. To make sure no witness is ever missing, the חכמים required the witnesses on every גט to sign together.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
All of you; the husband tells all the witnesses to sign

steps.whatToRemember: Signing together on a גט is a rabbinic גזירה, made because of the case where the husband said 'all of you.'

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is a decree because of “all of you.”
phrases.notes: The husband told a group 'all of you sign,' so if even one does not sign, the גט is not valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם כּוּלְּכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a rabbinic decree, made so that the case of a husband saying 'all of you' is handled correctly

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: Only One Samaritan Witness Is Allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that a גט was made valid only when just one of its witnesses is a כותי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself. רבי אלעזר said: They only allowed a גט with one כותי witness, and no more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a statement of רבי אלעזר that it mentioned earlier, and now studies it on its own. He says a גט is valid only if just one witness is a כותי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made an exception for a גט, allowing a כותי witness. רבי אלעזר sets a limit on that exception: one כותי witness is fine, but not both witnesses. This sets up the next question about why he needed to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to study a statement it quoted earlier
They made it valid
A Samaritan
One witness

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Elazar said:
They did not make it valid
except with just one Samaritan witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי אלעזר's statement, which was quoted earlier, to study it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט is valid with only one כותי witness, not two.

steps.title: Isn't This Already in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אלעזר adds, since the משנה already speaks of 'a כותי witness' in the singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned in the משנה: Any document that has a כותי witness on it is invalid, except a גט and a slave's release document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: his rule seems to be already in the משנה, so why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'a כותי witness', using the word for one. That already seems to mean only one כותי is allowed on a גט. So רבי אלעזר's statement looks like it adds nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (What does this add?)
We already learned it in a משנה
Invalid

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל גֵּט שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵד כּוּתִי –
phrases.english: Any document that has a Samaritan witness on it
is invalid, etc.!
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה: except a גט for a wife and a release document for a slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 8 adds anything beyond the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already uses the singular 'a כותי witness', so the limit of one seems already known.

steps.title: Without רבי אלעזר, We Might Allow Two
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה alone we might allow two כותי witnesses. The singular wording could just be stressing that other documents can't have even one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the משנה, I would have said a גט is valid even with two כותי witnesses. I would have thought the משנה said 'one' only to show that other documents are invalid with even one. So רבי אלעזר teaches us that only one is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's wording could be read another way, so רבי אלעזר is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'one' in the משנה might be aimed at other documents: even a single כותי witness ruins them. If so, the משנה says nothing about how many are allowed on a גט. רבי אלעזר settles it: on a גט, only one.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (what we might have mistakenly thought)
Two
Documents (other legal papers)
He teaches us (this is the new point)

phrases.english: If it were from the mishna alone,
I would have said even two are also fine;
and the fact that it teaches 'one'
is because for other documents
even one is also not allowed;
so he teaches us.
phrases.notes: He teaches us that on a גט, only one כותי witness is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the משנה's wording could be read differently, so the statement is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two כותי witnesses are fine on a גט. The singular only teaches that one ruins other documents.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one כותי witness is allowed on a גט.

steps.title: But רבן גמליאל Accepted Samaritan Witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר from the משנה's story: רבן גמליאל accepted a גט whose witnesses were כותים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are two really not allowed? But the משנה teaches: A woman's גט was once brought before רבן גמליאל in כפר עותנאי. Its witnesses were כותי witnesses, and he ruled it valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's rule with a story from the משנה. In that story, more than one כותי witness seems to have signed and the גט was accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story says 'its witnesses', in the plural, were כותים. That sounds like both witnesses. If רבן גמליאל accepted that גט, it clashes with the rule that only one כותי is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches (a challenge from a source)
An incident or story
The village of Otnai
Its witnesses (plural)

phrases.english: And two are not allowed?!
But it teaches: An incident occurred
and they brought before Rabban Gamliel
in the village of Otnai a woman's bill of divorce,
and its witnesses were Samaritan witnesses,
and he ruled it valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 10 that two כותים are not allowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only one כותי witness is allowed on a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's story uses the plural 'its witnesses were כותים', and רבן גמליאל still accepted the גט.

steps.title: אביי: Read It as 'Its Witness'
steps.stepSummary: אביי changes the reading of the story to the singular, 'its witness', so only one כותי signed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Read the story as 'its witness', meaning only one witness was a כותי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by changing one word in the story, from plural to singular.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we read 'its witness', then רבן גמליאל accepted a גט with only one כותי witness. That fits רבי אלעזר's rule exactly. On this reading, רבן גמליאל does not argue with anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Read it as (change the wording of the source)
Its witness (singular)

phrases.english: Abaye said,
read it as: 'Its witness.'
phrases.notes: Instead of 'its witnesses' in the plural, read the singular, so only one witness was a כותי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by changing the wording of the story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story speaks of two כותי witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story speaks of one כותי witness, so it fits רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: רבא: רבן גמליאל Argues and Allows Two
steps.stepSummary: רבא keeps the story as two כותי witnesses. He says רבן גמליאל argues with the first opinion, and the משנה is missing a line stating his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The story really is about two witnesses, and רבן גמליאל disagrees. The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: 'And רבן גמליאל allows a גט with two כותי witnesses. There was also a story where a woman's גט was brought before רבן גמליאל in כפר עותנאי, its witnesses were כותים, and he ruled it valid.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer from אביי. He does not change the word in the story. Instead, he adds a missing line to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the first opinion in the משנה holds like רבי אלעזר: only one כותי is allowed. רבן גמליאל disagrees and allows two, and the story is his proof. So the story no longer challenges רבי אלעזר, because it shows a different opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually (keep the original reading)
He disagrees
The משנה is missing words
And this is what it teaches (the fuller wording)

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the story of רבן גמליאל. אביי: read 'its witness', so there was only one כותי and nobody argues. רבא: it really was two כותים, and רבן גמליאל argues with the first opinion, as the missing line in the משנה shows.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying רבי אלעזר is wrong. רבי אלעזר follows the first opinion in the משנה, and רבן גמליאל simply holds a different view.

phrases.english: Rava said: Actually, it was two,
and Rabban Gamliel disagrees;
phrases.notes: He disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה, which allows only one.

phrases.english: and the mishna is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
And Rabban Gamliel rules it valid with two,
and there was also an incident in which they brought
before Rabban Gamliel in the village of Otnai

phrases.aramaic: גֵּט אִשָּׁה, וְהָיוּ עֵדָיו עֵדֵי כוּתִים,
phrases.english: a woman's bill of divorce, and its witnesses were Samaritan witnesses,
and he ruled it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from אביי's in step 12 to the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a missing line to the משנה, making it an argument between the first opinion and רבן גמליאל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story challenges the rule of only one כותי witness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story follows רבן גמליאל, who allows two. The first opinion, like רבי אלעזר, allows only one.

steps.title: Documents from non-Jewish courts are valid, except a גט and a slave's freedom document
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that documents produced in non-Jewish courts are valid even if non-Jews signed them. The exceptions are a גט for a woman and a document freeing a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: All documents that come before non-Jewish courts are valid, even though non-Jews signed them. The exceptions are a woman's גט and a document freeing a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a general rule that documents from non-Jewish courts are accepted, with two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we need Jewish witnesses, so it is surprising that non-Jewish signatures are good enough. The משנה still leaves out a גט and a slave's freedom document. The משנה does not say why these two are different; the גמרא discusses that in the coming steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
Legal documents
Non-Jewish courts
Divorce documents for women
Documents that free slaves

phrases.english: MISHNA:
All documents that come up
phrases.notes: Literally 'that go up.' It means documents brought before the court and made there.

phrases.english: in courts of non-Jews
even though their signers are non-Jews
are valid
except for divorce documents of women
and documents freeing slaves

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַשְּׁטָרוֹת הָעוֹלִים בְּעַרְכָּאוֹת שֶׁל גּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of רבי אלעזר and the כותי witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Documents from non-Jewish courts are valid, except a גט and a slave's freedom document.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says even a גט and a freedom document from such courts are valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion. He says the exceptions apply only when a private person made those documents, not a court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Even these are valid. They were mentioned as exceptions only for when they were made by a private person.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה argues with the first. רבי שמעון makes the exception much smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, a גט or freedom document made in a non-Jewish court is valid as well. The only invalid case is when a private non-Jew wrote and signed it outside of court.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion here
A private, ordinary person (not a court)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says
Even these are valid
they were mentioned only
when they were made by a private person
phrases.notes: He means a document a private non-Jew wrote and signed, not one made in a court.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף אֵלּוּ כְּשֵׁירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the exception in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט and a freedom document made in a non-Jewish court are also valid. Only those made by a private person are invalid.

steps.title: The משנה makes no difference between a sale and a gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה's rule is general. It covers sale documents and gift documents alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The משנה states the rule without any division. It makes no difference whether the document is for a sale or for a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an observation about how broad the משנה is. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'all documents' include every kind of transaction. The גמרא highlights this because a gift will turn out to be harder to explain than a sale.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
He states the rule as a clear, general rule with no divisions
It makes no difference

phrases.english: GEMARA:
He teaches it as a sweeping rule
no difference whether a sale
or a gift

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the wide wording of the משנה in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's approval covers both sale documents and gift documents.

steps.title: A sale is easy to explain: the money transfers ownership and the document is only proof
steps.stepSummary: With a sale, the buyer acquires the item when he pays in front of the court. The document only proves that the payment happened. The court would not risk its good name by writing a false document.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a sale. Once the buyer pays money in front of them, he has acquired the item, and the document is just proof. If he had not paid in front of them, they would not hurt their own reputation by writing him a document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the rule works for a sale. This is the first half of a 'בשלמא' setup, and the hard question about a gift comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sale, the payment is what transfers ownership, not the document. The non-Jewish court can be trusted that the payment happened, because writing a false document would damage the court's reputation. So the document only needs to work as proof.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable (opens a comparison before a question)
Money, coins
Merely proof
Harm themselves (damage their own reputation)

phrases.english: It is understandable with a sale
from when he gives money in front of them
that is when he acquired it
and the document is merely proof
for if he had not given money in front of them
they would not harm themselves
phrases.notes: He means the court would not ruin its good name by writing a false document.

phrases.english: and write him a document

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the easy case (a sale) before challenging the hard case (a gift).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a sale, the payment transfers ownership and the non-Jewish document only serves as reliable proof.

steps.title: A gift is a problem: the document itself transfers it, but a non-Jewish document is worthless
steps.stepSummary: With a gift, no money is paid. The document itself must transfer ownership. But a document made by non-Jews has no legal power, so it is like a broken piece of pottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a gift, how is it acquired? Isn't it through this document? And this document is just a piece of broken pottery!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule for gift documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sale, the document only needs to prove what happened. In a gift, the document is the act of acquiring, so it must be a valid document. A document made by non-Jews is not a valid document according to הלכה, so the gift should not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: By what means does he acquire?
Merely a piece of broken pottery (worthless)

phrases.english: But a gift
by what does he acquire it
is it not through this document
and this document is merely a piece of pottery

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the gift with the sale from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that gift documents from non-Jewish courts are valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gift is acquired through the document itself, and a non-Jewish document has no halachic power, so the gift should not take effect.

steps.title: שמואל: the law of the kingdom is the law
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the law of the government is binding. Since the kingdom's law recognizes these documents, they really do transfer the gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The law of the kingdom is the law.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question about gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The document gets its power from the law of the kingdom, not from the signers being kosher witnesses. Because the government accepts this way of transferring property, הלכה accepts it too, so the gift document works.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer
The law of the kingdom is the law (government law is binding)

steps.whatToRemember: A sale document from a non-Jewish court works as proof, because the payment already transferred ownership. A gift document works because of דינא דמלכותא דינא.
steps.whyThisMatters: דינא דמלכותא דינא becomes a major principle for how halacha relates to the laws of the government.

phrases.english: Shmuel said
The law of the kingdom is the law

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new principle that gives the document its legal power
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A gift document from non-Jews is worthless, so the gift cannot take effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The kingdom's law gives the document power, so the gift takes effect.

steps.title: A second answer: read the משנה as 'except for documents like divorce documents'
steps.stepSummary: Instead of relying on שמואל's rule, the גמרא suggests changing the wording of the משנה. The exception covers every document that does a legal act by itself, like a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say that the משנה should be taught: 'except for documents that are like גיטי נשים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to solve the problem of gift documents from step 18. It changes the wording of the משנה so that gift documents are no longer counted as valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 kept gift documents valid by using דינא דמלכותא דינא. Here the גמרא takes the other road. Only documents that just prove something, like a sale document, are valid. Any document that makes the legal change itself, like a גט or a gift document, belongs to the exception and is invalid from a non-Jewish court.

keyTerms.meaning: If you prefer, say: introduces another possible answer
Teach it this way: a change in how the text is read
Like divorce documents: documents that do the legal act themselves

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rule added to step 19. It is a different answer. In this answer gift documents from non-Jewish courts are invalid, not valid.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: teach
"except for those like bills of divorce."
phrases.notes: The small letter כ means 'like'. So the exception now covers any document that works like a גט, including a gift document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the קשיא of step 18, in place of שמואל's answer in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's general rule makes all documents from non-Jewish courts valid, gift documents too, even though they have no power to transfer ownership.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exception covers every document that does the legal act itself. So gift documents are invalid, and only proof documents like sales are valid.

steps.title: How can רבי שמעון accept גיטין from non-Jews?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's view in the משנה and asks how it can be right. Non-Jews have no part in the laws of divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי שמעון says even these are valid. But non-Jews are not part of the laws of 'severance' (divorce)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the end of the משנה and quotes רבי שמעון. Then it challenges him right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says even גיטין and slave-freeing documents signed by non-Jews are valid. But the Torah's laws of marriage and divorce were given only to Jews. So how can non-Jews play any role in making a גט work?

keyTerms.meaning: Valid, acceptable
People who belong to the laws of divorce (a גט is called a 'document of severance')

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even these are valid, etc.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the גיטין and the documents freeing slaves that the first opinion left out.

phrases.english: But they are not subject to the laws of severance?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of sale and gift documents and starts a new question about רבי שמעון's view in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that גיטין signed by non-Jews are valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Non-Jews are outside the laws of divorce, so their signatures should not be able to make a גט valid.

steps.title: רבי שמעון follows רבי אלעזר: the witnesses to the handing over make the גט work
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that for רבי שמעון the signatures on the גט don't matter. What makes the divorce happen is the witnesses who watch the גט being handed over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: רבי שמעון follows the view of רבי אלעזר, who said that the witnesses to the handing over are the ones who make the divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge from step 21. He links רבי שמעון to the well-known view of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, the divorce happens when the גט is handed to the woman in front of witnesses. The signatures are not the key part. So it does not matter that the signers were non-Jews, because the real witnesses are the ones watching the handover.

keyTerms.meaning: Went along with his approach, followed his view
Witnesses to the handing over of the גט
They cut, meaning they make the divorce take effect

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the two possible bases for a גט: the signing witnesses or the witnesses to the handover. That idea comes up again and again in מסכת גיטין.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira says:

phrases.aramaic: יָרַד רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְשִׁיטָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon went down to the approach of Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: Literally 'went down', meaning he went along with רבי אלעזר's view.

phrases.english: who says the witnesses of the transmission effect the divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: יָרַד רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְשִׁיטָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the view to another תנא's known opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גט depends on its signers, so signers who are non-Jews should make it invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אלעזר the handover witnesses make the divorce. So the signers don't matter, and רבי שמעון can accept a גט signed by non-Jews.

steps.title: But רבי אלעזר agrees that a built-in forgery makes the גט invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא with a teaching of רבי אבא. Even רבי אלעזר says a גט with bad signatures written on it is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אבא said: רבי אלעזר agrees that a document forged from within is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי זירא's answer from step 22. It uses a limit on רבי אלעזר's view that רבי אבא reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר does not need signatures on a גט. But if the גט does have signatures and they are invalid, the document is 'forged from within', and he agrees it is invalid. Signatures of non-Jews on a גט should count as exactly that kind of bad signature, so the link to רבי אלעזר seems not to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, admits
Forged from within: a document whose own signatures are invalid
Invalid

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forged from within' does not have to mean someone faked a name. It means the document itself carries invalid signatures, even if the handover was done properly.

phrases.english: But doesn't Rabbi Abba say:
Rabbi Elazar concedes
regarding a document forged from within, that it is invalid!
phrases.notes: He means the signatures written on the גט are themselves invalid, so the paper carries its own flaw.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בִּמְזוּיָּף מִתּוֹכוֹ, שֶׁפָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that רבי שמעון's view fits רבי אלעזר's
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even רבי אלעזר says invalid signatures on a גט make it invalid. Signatures of non-Jews are invalid signatures, so the גט should still be invalid.

steps.title: The גמרא begins its answer: what case are we talking about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its reply to רבי אבא's challenge by saying it will explain what case רבי שמעון means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to answer the challenge from step 23 by narrowing the case, and the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'what are we dealing with here' tells us the גמרא will not drop רבי זירא's answer. It will describe a specific case in which non-Jewish signatures do not count as a forgery inside the document.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here: introduces a narrowing of the case

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (the answer continues in the next part of the text)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון means any גט signed by non-Jews, which would be forged from within.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גמרא is about to explain a specific case where רבי שמעון's ruling still fits רבי אלעזר.
